Definition: of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard):--title.
BiblicalUsage: Pilate wrote a title and put it on the cross: JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS. Many of the Jews read the title, written in Hebrew and Greek and Latin, and the placard meant for shame became the first public proclamation of the crucified King.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title is the gospel in three languages at once: what Pilate meant as a charge, God used as a confession.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
